summary: Gyoshu Chujo was a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1996) and Minobusan University (attested 2001).
Gyu Eon Jang works in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding posts as a professor at Peking University and as an HK research professor at Geumgang University (attested 2015).

Gyurme Dorje (1950–2020) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and SOAS, completing his PhD under Philip Denwood. He also studied under several traditional teachers and served as a research fellow at SOAS (~1991–1996).

György Hazai (1932–2016) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1949–1954) and held a post at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1963–1983).
György Kara (1935–2022) specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (~1953–1958), he held a post at Indiana University (~1993–2022).

Gérard Colas is an Indologist who served as a research director and senior fellow at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009) and as a CNRS research director at École des hautes études en sciences sociales (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman (1940–2022) was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at École Normale Supérieure (~1961–1965), he succeeded Jean Filliozat and served as a professor at Collège de France (~1984–2011, attested 2012).

Géza Bethlenfalvy (1936–2021) studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Louis Ligeti. A scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at ELTE (~1976–2005), the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, Delhi, and Vienna.
Gösta Liebert (1916–1998) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held a post at the University of Gothenburg from circa 1956 to 1982.

Götz von Selle (1893–1956) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Kiel, and the University of Göttingen (~1920–1923), later holding a post at the University of Göttingen (~1928–1938).
Günter Grönbold is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served at the Bavarian State Library from circa 1974 to 2008, where he was Head of the South Asia Department.

Günter Schweiger is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (~1960–1965) and under Gert Klingenschmitt (~1998–2002), serving on the faculty at WU Vienna (~1974–2010).

Indologist H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where C. Kunhan Raja supervised his MA. By 1944, he held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre and the University of Madras.
H. V. Nagaraja Rao is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Hachiro Hasebe is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Keio University (~1969–1973), he served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University (~1993–1999).
Haeju Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Kemu Jin and under Zhongxin Jiang, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and as Director at the University of Freiburg.

Hajime Kitamura (1923–2003) was a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at Shizuoka High School and the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, NINJAL, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Reitaku University.

Hajime Nakamura (1912–1999) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (1936). He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1943–1973) and founded and directed the Eastern Institute/Toho Gakuin (~1973–1999).

Hajime Okayama (1948–2022) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1977) and under Xianlin Ji (~1979–1981), later serving as professor at the University of Tokyo and at its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
